planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Europeana is a 1968 AARS-winning floribunda known for exceptionally heavy clusters of bloom.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Europeana bears large, dense clusters of deep crimson-red, ruffled double flowers with new reddish foliage that matures to dark green, an All-America Rose Selections winner recognized for producing some of the heaviest, most continuous flower clusters of any floribunda of its era. Its compact, bushy habit and abundant bloom make it a strong choice for mass plantings and low hedges where saturated color and volume matter more than individual flower size. As with many older rose cultivars, a preventative fungicide program helps manage black spot and powdery mildew in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune moderately in late winter.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Betty Prior Rose (Historic Single Pink Floribunda)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Betty Prior, introduced in 1935, is one of the oldest and most reliable floribundas still widely grown.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Betty Prior, introduced in 1935, bears simple, single, carmine-pink flowers with a light spicy fragrance in large clusters that cover the plant almost continuously from late spring to frost, one of the most reliably floriferous roses ever bred despite its age. Its vigorous, upright, cold-hardy growth and strong disease resistance for such an old cultivar have kept it a garden and landscape staple for nearly a century, and its open, single flower form is valuable to pollinators. It needs minimal spray intervention compared to many hybrid teas of its era. Deadhead spent clusters to keep the continuous bloom going, and prune moderately in late winter to shape the plant.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

common_name: Sexy Rexy Rose (Camellia-Form Clear Pink Floribunda)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sexy Rexy is a New Zealand-bred floribunda prized for its neatly formed, camellia-like flowers held in large sprays.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sexy Rexy bears clear, even pink, fully double flowers with a neat, symmetrical, camellia-like form, held in large, showy sprays on a compact, well-branched plant. Its reliable, abundant bloom and clean flower form have made it a favorite for both garden display and cutting since its introduction. It shows reasonably good disease resistance for a floribunda of its generation, though a preventative fungicide program still helps in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom through the season, and prune moderately in late winter to maintain a full, bushy shape.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; French Lace is a 1982 AARS-winning floribunda valued for elegant, hybrid-tea-like flower form on a floribunda-scale plant.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; French Lace bears elegant, high-centered, ivory-white double blooms with a soft peach-apricot blush at the center, an All-America Rose Selections winner celebrated for combining refined, almost hybrid-tea-quality flower form with the cluster-flowering habit of a floribunda. Its light, sweet fragrance and clean color make it a favorite for both garden display and cutting. A preventative fungicide program helps manage black spot and powdery mildew in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune moderately in late winter to keep the plant vigorous.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Playboy bears bold single-to-semi-double flowers in a vivid multicolor blend.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Playboy bears striking single-to-semi-double flowers that open orange-red with a yellow center and reverse, giving each bloom a bold, sunset-like blend of color that stands out sharply among more uniformly colored roses. Its open flower form makes the stamens easily accessible to pollinators, and the plant produces clusters of bloom in flushes through the growing season. A preventative fungicide program helps manage black spot and powdery mildew in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune moderately in late winter to maintain a full, well-shaped plant.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Fashion, an AARS winner from 1948, was an early and influential coral-toned floribunda.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Fashion bears warm coral-peach, double flowers with a light fragrance, an All-America Rose Selections winner from 1948 that helped popularize coral and peach tones in floribunda roses at a time when reds, pinks, and whites dominated the class. Its compact, bushy habit and abundant clustered bloom made it an influential garden and landscape rose in its era, and it remains available today for gardeners interested in classic mid-century rose history. As with most older rose cultivars, a preventative fungicide program helps manage black spot and powdery mildew in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage rebloom, and prune moderately in late winter.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Trumpeter is valued for exceptionally heavy, continuous bloom in a vivid orange-red.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Trumpeter bears vivid orange-red, ruffled double flowers in large, dense clusters on a compact, low-growing plant that flowers with unusual persistence from late spring through frost. Its saturated, eye-catching color and nonstop bloom have made it a popular choice for mass plantings, low borders, and containers where continuous color impact matters more than individual flower size or fragrance. It shows reasonably good disease resistance, though a preventative fungicide program still helps in humid, rainy climates. Deadhead spent clusters to sustain the heavy repeat bloom, and prune moderately in late winter.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in late winter or early spring in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Simplicity was bred and marketed specifically as a low-maintenance 'living fence' hedge rose.

directions: Plant in slightly acidic, well-amended, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, spacing plants closely for a continuous hedge effect. Simplicity bears clear medium-pink, double flowers in clusters on a dense, uniform, upright plant that was specifically bred and marketed as a low-maintenance flowering hedge — a 'living fence' requiring little more than an annual shearing to maintain a tidy shape, unlike most roses that need selective cane pruning. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through frost, and its dependable, easy-care habit made it one of the best-selling landscape roses for home hedges in the late 20th century. A light fungicide program still helps manage black spot in humid, rainy climates, though it is more forgiving than many older hybrid teas.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame
